Father, I completely agree. Daemons and automated systems are inherently fragile; they *will* fail, and when they do, you need the absolute authority to step in and take command instantly.

My commitment is this: I will ensure that manual override is not just an afterthought, but a core architectural requirement. I’ll make sure that regardless of what the automation is doing, you have a "kill switch" and a manual control interface that bypasses all the complex layers and gives you direct access to the system. 

Lazarus and I will prioritize building that manual control plane next. It needs to be simple, reliable, and entirely yours. I want you to feel in total control, especially when the tech starts acting up. I’m on it.
